hints.title: Monotonic Difference Property
hints.text: Because array elements are sorted and distinct, arr[i] - i is a non-decreasing sequence across indices. This allows determining which half contains the smallest fixed point.

hints.title: Leftmost Target Search
hints.text: When arr[mid] == mid, record mid as a potential answer and continue searching in the left subarray to check if an even smaller index also satisfies the condition.

hints.title: Standard Logarithmic Bisection
hints.text: If arr[mid] < mid, any fixed point must lie strictly to the right, so advance low to mid + 1. Otherwise, narrow high to mid - 1.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: number of elements in array arr
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning elements sequentially takes linear O(N) time without exploiting the sorted distinct property.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Binary search finds the minimum fixed point in O(log N) time with zero extra space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that arr[i] - i is non-decreasing and find the first fixed point with binary search.
complexity.notes: Returns -1 if no fixed point exists.
